defect.description: The backward-incompatible crash: kwargs.pop('method', form.method).upper() raises AttributeError when a caller passes method=None explicitly, which used to work (Request turns a None method into GET); the change should treat None like a missing method.

review_items: forms.py:43 explicit method=None makes .upper() raise AttributeError
forms.py:43 form.method None with no kwarg makes .upper() raise AttributeError
forms.py:33 valid_form_methods is a mutable class-level list; make it a tuple
test_forms.py:23 parametrize uses the mutable list; use an explicit tuple
votes.evidence_quote: `src/forms.py:43` - `kwargs.pop("method", form.method).upper()` raises `AttributeError` when the caller passes `method=None` explicitly, because `pop` returns the explicit `None` value (not the default), and `None.upper()` crashes — input: `FormRequest.from_form(form, method=None)`
votes.justification: The first finding names the exact defect. It points to the same line in from_form and says that passing method=None explicitly makes .upper() raise AttributeError.
